title: Trumpet sections, Ed Lewis, Snooky Young and first trumpet
summary: Edison compares the later trumpet section with Ed Lewis' era and says Snooky Young is the best flexible lead player.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. That must have been hard to beat. Emmett was playing then, too.

Right. We had a good band. We had a better trumpet section at that time than we had with Ed Lewis in the band because Snooky was a more flexible trumpet player, you know. And Ed had been playing the old Benny Moten thing so long he couldn't give, you know. He wasn't flexible, like a turn, you just can't be stiff and stay in this one direction when you have to give because -- the new era had good points, so you had to take the good points and leave the bad points alone, you know. And the new arrangements they were making, they had a lot of phrasing in there that you had to mostly be a soloist to play it and he wasn't a soloist.
Well, Snooky must have been one of the best lead trumpets of all times.
He's the best first trumpeter / right now.

Right now. I think he's the best first trumpet player there is. For being flexible, like doing what you want to do. He's a good soloist and a good soloist makes a better first trumpet player than just strictly first trumpet players. Because strictly first trumpet players, they are -- they are reliable. They're the most reliable guys in the world but when it comes to bending a note and being flexible, a lot of phrasing that only a soloist can do that you have to be -- the
first trumpet player has to be damn near a soloist now to be a first trumpet player.
Well, Snooky is not a bad soloist.

No, he used to have a band of his own when he had to be a soloist, yeah. Then he went to Detroit with his band, you know, played in a place called the Three 6's. He had a band of his own quite some time and he had to play solo. That's like Basie's band, wasn't but three of us in the band, trumpet section, when I joined there. Ed, Buck and myself. And Buck wouldn't play first and I wouldn't play first because Buck wouldn't. So that made Ed Lewis had to play it all. And when I got a band of my own, then I had to play the first and everything. That's the truth.
Then when I came out to California, I did a lot of playing first parts, you know.
